primary_citation.popular_name: Hate Crime — Interference with Rights by Force or Threat

key_holding: No person — whether or not acting under color of law — may by force or threat of force willfully injure, intimidate, interfere with, oppress, or threaten any person in the free exercise of constitutional or statutory rights because of actual or perceived characteristics (race, gender, sexual orientation, etc. per §422.55). CRITICAL SPEECH PROTECTION: Subdivision (c) provides that 'a person shall not be convicted of violating subdivision (a) based upon speech alone, except upon a showing that the speech itself threatened violence against a specific person or group of persons and that the defendant had the apparent ability to carry out the threat.' This is the speech-alone exception — pure speech cannot be the basis of a §422.6 conviction absent a true-threat showing.

amendment_history.event: Stats. 2011, Ch. 15, Sec. 345. Effective April 4, 2011. Operative October 1, 2011.
